cards.text: Meet John the Baptist, the man who baptized crowds in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:5-6). Right now he's in prison, and from in there he hears about the works of Christ. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, so I KNOW that life: stuck in the dark, getting all the news secondhand.

cards.question: John can't walk out of prison to see Jesus for himself. Who does he send to Jesus with a question?
John's disciples reach Jesus with John's question. What does John want to know?

answers.text: If Jesus is the One who was to come
If Jesus will come to the prison
If Jesus will teach his disciples

cards.text: Jesus doesn't just hand them a yes. He tells John's disciples, "Go back and report to John what you hear and see:"
Here's the report: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear. John sent a yes or no question, and Jesus sent back a WHOLE highlight reel.

cards.question: True or false: part of Jesus' report for John is that the dead are raised.
In that same report for John, Jesus says the good news is preached to the ___.
Jesus ends His message for John with a blessing. Who is the blessing for?

answers.text: Whoever doesn't fall away because of Him
Whoever gives to the poor in secret
Whoever keeps watch through the night

cards.text: As John's disciples are leaving, Jesus starts talking to the crowds about John. He asks them, "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?"

cards.question: Next, Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a man dressed in fine clothes. He says people who wear fine clothing are found in ___.
Then Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a prophet. True or false: Jesus says John is a prophet and nothing more.
Jesus says John is the one it is written about: a messenger sent on ahead. That messenger is sent to ___ the way.
Jesus keeps talking to the crowds about John. True or false: Jesus says no one born of women has risen greater than John the Baptist.
Then Jesus adds a twist: someone IS greater than John. Who does He name?

answers.text: The least in the kingdom of heaven
The angels who stand before God

cards.text: Friend, this next one's heavy, so read it slow: Jesus says that from the days of John the Baptist until now, "the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it." And all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John, right up to the man sitting in that prison cell.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowds that if they're willing to accept it, John is the ___ who was to come.

cards.text: Jesus says, "He who has ears, let him hear." Then He asks what He can compare this generation to, and He paints a picture from the marketplace.

cards.question: In Jesus' marketplace picture of this generation, who is sitting there calling out to others?

cards.text: The children call out, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn." That's like baking a soft batch for someone who won't touch it, so you bake a crunchy batch, and they won't touch THAT either.

cards.question: Jesus says John came neither eating nor drinking. What do people say about John?
Then Jesus, the Son of Man, came eating and drinking. True or false: this time, the people finally approve.

cards.text: They say, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" And Jesus ends with this: "But wisdom is vindicated by her actions."

findings.problem: The passage opens mid-thought with "Meanwhile", but the opening card never sets up the context. It doesn't say what Jesus has been doing (Matthew 11:1: teaching and preaching in their towns), and it doesn't say who "Christ" is the first time He appears. The joke takes the third sentence, so the context gets no room.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "Here's the report:" followed by four items reads like the whole report. A thoughtful baker would then mark card 6 ("the dead are raised") False. The setup steers the baker away from the right answer instead of letting them reason toward it. The card should signal that the list keeps going, or not frame it as the full report.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The two wrong answers are near-twins: "The angels who stand before God" and "The cherubim around God's throne" are both heavenly beings near God's throne. The right answer is the only different kind of answer. The "twist" setup also points to the surprising option. Together, these make the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Story card 5 only says Jesus "paints a picture from the marketplace." Nothing points to children over merchants or soldiers, so getting it right is luck. Stop 2 already leans on discovery questions (cards 1, 4 and 8). This one could be made reasonable by giving context, like people calling out to others to join in a game, without saying who they are.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice is thin through most of the walkthrough. After stop 1 card 5 the cards are mostly plain retelling. Stop 1 cards 9 to 12 and stop 2 cards 1 to 6 have no laugh, even though moments like the reed swaying in the wind and the man in fine clothes could hold one without muddying a fact. The one joke in stop 2 (card 7, soft batch and crunchy batch) is mild.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
